reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / GOLD & ATS guidelines
clinicalPearls: Presents with progressive exertional breathlessness and a persistent dry cough, often over months to years
Fine bibasal end-inspiratory crackles (often described as Velcro-like) and finger clubbing are characteristic examination findings
High-resolution CT showing a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern, with subpleural and basal reticulation, traction bronchiectasis, and honeycombing, is central to diagnosis
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is a diagnosis of exclusion requiring careful evaluation for connective tissue disease, drug toxicity, and environmental or occupational exposures
Pulmonary function tests typically show a restrictive pattern with reduced lung volumes and impaired gas transfer (low DLCO)
Multidisciplinary discussion combining clinical, radiological, and where needed histological data improves diagnostic accuracy
Antifibrotic therapy can slow the decline in lung function in IPF; supportive measures include oxygen, pulmonary rehabilitation, and vaccination
Acute exacerbations cause rapid deterioration and carry high mortality; lung transplantation should be considered in suitable candidates
reference.pathophysiology: Repeated microinjury to the alveolar epithelium in a susceptible (often ageing, genetically predisposed) individual triggers aberrant wound-healing rather than normal repair. Activated fibroblasts and myofibroblasts accumulate in fibroblastic foci and deposit excess extracellular matrix, progressively distorting and stiffening the lung architecture. The result is loss of functional alveolar units, honeycomb cystic change, impaired gas exchange, and reduced compliance, producing a restrictive physiology with worsening hypoxaemia.
additionalDifferentials: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease
Pneumoconioses such as asbestosis or silicosis
Chronic left heart failure with interstitial oedema
additionalInvestigations: High-resolution CT of the chest to assess for a UIP pattern and distribution of fibrosis
Full pulmonary function testing including spirometry, lung volumes, and diffusing capacity
Serological screen for connective tissue disease and, where indicated, hypersensitivity precipitins
Six-minute walk test with oximetry to assess functional impairment and desaturation
Surgical or transbronchial lung biopsy in selected cases where imaging is non-diagnostic
redFlags: Rapid worsening of dyspnoea with new diffuse ground-glass change suggesting an acute exacerbation
Resting hypoxaemia or significant desaturation on exertion
Signs of pulmonary hypertension or right heart failure
Features suggesting an underlying treatable systemic disease that alter management
reference.prognosis: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is generally progressive with a poor prognosis and median survival of only a few years from diagnosis, though the course is variable; antifibrotic drugs slow decline and transplantation can prolong survival in eligible patients, while acute exacerbations markedly worsen outcome.
pitfalls: Labelling fibrosis as idiopathic without excluding occupational, drug, and connective tissue causes
Using corticosteroids or immunosuppression indiscriminately in IPF, where they may be harmful
Missing coexisting emphysema, which can mask spirometric restriction
Delaying transplant referral until the patient is too deconditioned to be a candidate
management: Antifibrotic therapy with pirfenidone or nintedanib to slow decline in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and other progressive fibrosing phenotypes
Treat identifiable causes, using immunosuppression for connective tissue disease-related fibrosis, antigen avoidance in hypersensitivity pneumonitis, and withdrawal of culprit drugs
Long-term oxygen therapy for hypoxaemia and pulmonary rehabilitation to improve function
Symptom control for breathlessness and cough with early integration of palliative care
Manage comorbidities including gastro-oesophageal reflux, pulmonary hypertension and obstructive sleep apnoea, and keep vaccinations up to date
Serial pulmonary function and diffusing capacity with multidisciplinary review to monitor progression
Recognise and treat acute exacerbations, which markedly worsen prognosis, with supportive care and corticosteroids, and refer eligible patients for lung transplantation assessment
